brief:
Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said anti-Turkey discourse is intensifying as Israeli elections approach, Shehab Wire reported. Fidan characterized Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a threat extending beyond the region itself, though his full remarks were not completely preserved in available accounts of the statement.

The comments reflect mounting tensions between Ankara and Jerusalem ahead of the ballot. Fidan's assertion that anti-Turkey messaging is accelerating in the campaign suggests Turkey views the election environment as a driver of hostility toward the country. The timing of his remarks underscores Turkish concern over political rhetoric in Israel as voters prepare to cast ballots.
